headline: Spatial methods separate composition, state and niche; trajectory models add mechanism
label: Spatial Attribution And Trajectory Inference
summary: Spatial tools now attribute expression to abundance, state, niche or single molecules; trajectory tools add GRNs, lineage barcodes and plausibility metrics.
synthesis: The dominant thread is attributing spatial transcriptomic variation to distinct sources. ARCADE separates cell-type abundance from continuous intratype state. SWIMR improves deconvolution by integrating multiple scRNA-seq references with spatial correlations. Tracel reassigns transcripts or bin counts to cells via two-stage optimal transport against matched references. FICTURE2 infers each RNA molecule's transcriptional program from gene identity and spatial context. Domain calling is becoming niche-aware: Kontext jointly embeds cells and local environments through ligand-receptor interactions, and smoothclust adds a boundary-density summary of label transitions. CRISP characterizes cross-signal interactions in single-cell and spatial data. LCM-Spatial-ATAC-seq in zonated hepatocytes separates an invariant cell-type sub-network from state-level regulation. A second thread makes trajectories mechanistic and testable: bowside couples trajectories with GRNs, ManifoldVelo jointly infers pseudotime and velocity, LOTUS uses lineage barcodes in unbalanced optimal transport, a Latent Cell-State Model treats transitions as a Markov chain, and BioTrajX scores biological plausibility. DynaCell and CardioShift address imaging-based single-cell phenotyping.
